comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
Using casefold below seems correct.
Should this actually be
```
if PY2:
    casefold = lamba x: x.upper().lower()
else:
    casefold = str.casefold
```

instead? `.upper().lower()` is kind of a "poor man's casefold" which will work for most things.

comments.author: author
comments.body: I can't say I really know my way around this.  What's an example of a thing that `.upper().lower()` covers in py2 that `.lower()` doesn't?  Since I don't know I don't care either way but figure I may as well learn.  `:]`

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
Sorry, I've misled you here. I'm not as clever as I think I am 😉 .

A case for casefold that I was thinking of is `ß`.
Uppercase `ß` should be `SS` -- I mean that in terms of how human languages, e.g. German, work -- so that `ß` and `ss` and `SS` all are treated as equivalent. But it seems that under py2, that's not how `upper()` on a unicode string behaves.

I don't think that case-folding on python2 is that reasonable to implement -- at least, not so trivial that it should simply be folded in here.

comments.author: author
comments.body:
I tried it with ß and saw py2 not doing anything at all with that regardless.  But, someone in `#python` found the example below to vary between `.lower()` and `.upper().lower()` when using Unicode.  The tests don't look to be using Unicode for choice though and the docstring doesn't even mention the expected type for the `choices` parameter so I don't know.  I'm fine with whatever (and it's already merged).  I suppose it could even be argued that my addition of using `str.casefold` at all is an unrelated change.  `:]`
